brief: A strawberry tower for a small balcony: one planter three storeys tall in the middle, ringed by six planters two storeys tall. Fill every planter with soil and plant strawberries in all seven, with a fruiting plant in the middle one.

requirements.requirement: One planter three storeys tall in the middle

requirements.evidence: six columns of 2x full bases at q,r ring; top cells hold bins
requirements.requirement: Ringed by six planters two storeys tall

requirements.evidence: fill_and_plant filled soil in all 7 bins
prop:1 strawberry-harvest in middle bin; props 2-7 strawberry-young in ring bins
requirements.requirement: Plant strawberries in all seven, with a fruiting plant in the middle one

finish.summary: Built a 7-cell tower: central 3-storey column with drained full bin on top, six 2-storey ring columns each with drained full bin on top. All 7 bins filled with soil; middle planted with fruiting (harvest-stage) strawberry, ring with young strawberries. House rules capped and locked; meshClash clear.

lines.label: Edge cap · male, two stories tall
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
